subject: Post-call: Cobalt Analytics — end-to-end tail latency & throughput qualification
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobalta.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cobalta.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Cobalt — end-to-end tail latency & throughput qualification

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard on the call
- Primary objective: migrate a mission-critical real-time insight endpoint from your current provider to Redwood with no regressions in tail latency (p95/p99) and equal-to-better throughput.
- Current provider summary (as shared): p95 ~ 350 ms, p99 ~ 1.2 s, sustained throughput 220 req/s at 128 avg tokens, observed streaming concurrency 40 sessions.
- Cobalt's acceptance window: p95 target ~ <= 200 ms, p99 target ~ <= 700 ms (tight for production), peak concurrency target ~ 120 concurrent streaming sessions, steady TPS target ~ 250 req/s.

Key unknowns we need you to confirm (can you reply inline?):
1) Request characteristics: typical prompt lengths (avg tokens), typical generation length and max tokens, and % of requests that use streaming vs non-streaming.
2) Network path: are these requests routed through an API gateway on your side? Any per-request proxying, WAF, or custom keep-alive settings?
3) SLA boundary: when you say p99 700 ms, are you measuring at client (browser/mobile) or at your edge proxy? We need to align measurement points for head-to-head qualification.

Proposed qualification plan (high-level)
- Phase A (today -> +5 business days): collect a representative request log (anonymized) and a 24-hour traces sample. You provide a request-log-sample.jsonl (see attachment names below).
- Phase B (+1 week): Redwood runs synthetic e2e tests that replay traffic (realistic interarrival and token distributions) against hosted API in our us-west region. We'll report p50/p95/p99 across cold, warm, and KV-cache-miss scenarios.
- Phase C (+2 weeks): joint PoC for a 48-72 hour soak with canary routing (5-10% traffic) and telemetry collection (per-token latency breakdown, network RTT, kernel time).

Acceptance criteria we propose (editable):
- p95 end-to-end (client-perceived) <= 200 ms for non-streaming requests (avg 128 tokens).
- p99 end-to-end <= 700 ms for same profile.
- Streaming: maintain ordered chunk delivery with per-chunk latency p95 <= 120 ms and p99 <= 400 ms; support 120 concurrent streaming sessions with < 5% error/retransmit.
- Throughput: sustained 250 req/s with end-to-end success rate >= 99.5%.

Attachments included for your convenience: redwood-e2e-slo-proposal.pdf (proposal + test matrix), redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx (metrics and measurement points), request-log-sample.jsonl (anonymized example format).

Next steps
- Alex/Priya: please confirm the three unknown items above and attach a 24-hr sample log.
- Marissa/Rishi: we'll scope the synthetic harness and estimate infra cost for the PoC.

Thanks — I'll coordinate scheduling once we have the sample log.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cobalta.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cobalt — end-to-end tail latency & throughput qualification

Jonas — thanks for the great write-up and the clear plan. Inline answers below and attaching a 24-hr sample as requested.

Inline: 
1) Request characteristics:
- Avg prompt tokens: 110 (range 45 - 420)
- Avg generation tokens: 90 (most below 150, some long-form to 512 occasionally)
- Streaming usage: 38% of requests use streaming (progressive UI; mostly small incremental tokens)

2) Network path:
- We route all calls through our edge proxy (edge.cobalta.com) which terminates TLS and forwards to providers. The proxy adds ~25-35 ms median; peaks to 80-120 ms on bad egress paths.
- No additional WAF rules beyond rate limiting; keep-alive is on (60s).

3) Measurement point:
- Our numbers are measured at the edge proxy (client-perceived). We can also capture client-side times. For PoC we can toggle measurement points but would like Redwood to run tests that mimic our edge (i.e., include a 30 ms fixed proxy RTT).

Attached: request-log-sample.jsonl (sanitized), sample traces, and a small network diagram (we'll upload to Drive link).

Open questions for Redwood team:
- Do you have tooling to replay streaming sessions faithfully (chunk boundaries + backpressure)?
- For p99 targets, how do you handle multi-tenant noisy neighbors? Any isolation/priority mechanisms in hosted?

We'll review the SOW draft and get back on signatures once we see the PoC cost estimate.

Thanks — Priya

Thanks for the ping — quick summary from infra side after reviewing the sample log: 

Findings / plan:
- Streaming replay: we can replay streaming sessions with accurate chunk boundaries and simulated client backpressure. Will use our harness (stream-replay-v2) and adapt inter-chunk timing distribution from the sample.
- Isolation: recommend a small dedicated shard (2 A100-equivalent GPUs) for the canary + autoscale policy capped at 6 GPUs for peak run. This gives dedicated compute and reduces noisy neighbor variance.
- Measurement points: will instrument both "backend perceived" (Redwood ingress) and "client-perceived" by adding a controlled 30 ms RTT shim in the replay harness to mimic edge.cobalta.com. We'll emit per-hop timing (proxy, network, token-gen, kernel).

Test matrix we will produce (deliverable):
- Synthetic replay: p50/p95/p99 across cold-start, warm, and KV-cache-miss paths; samples across 1k/10k/100k replayed requests.
- Streaming stress: step up concurrency 10 -> 120 sessions, monitor per-chunk latency distribution.
- Throughput soak: 24-hour 250 req/s soak (if customer greenlights full run) OR 48-72 hour 10% traffic soak for minimal risk.

Estimated timeline & owners:
- Today: confirm sample log receipt (done).
- +2 business days: infra config and quote for PoC (Rishi).
- +5 business days: synthetic replay report (Marissa/Rishi).
- +10 business days: 48-72 hour canary soak if approved.

Costs: early estimate attached in the redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx; will finalize after I size memory/kv-cache impact from the sample.

I'll prepare the test harness and share a runbook for the customer to approve measurement points.

— Rishi
Staff SWE, Redwood Inference
